tagline: OV-102 — the first Shuttle orbiter to fly to space (STS-1, 1981-04-12); lost on re-entry STS-107 2003-02-01
description: The first operational Space Shuttle orbiter. Flew 28 missions over 22 years including STS-1 (the first crewed test flight of a new American spacecraft in 25 years), the 1990 Astro-1 UV-astronomy mission, the 1993 SLS-2 life-sciences flight, and Senator John Glenn's STS-95 return-to-space in 1998. Lost on re-entry during STS-107 (2003-02-01) — a foam strike during launch breached the left wing's RCC leading edge and the vehicle disintegrated over Texas at Mach 18 with the loss of all seven crew. The accident grounded the Shuttle fleet for 29 months and triggered the Vision for Space Exploration.
best_known_for: First Shuttle orbiter to fly to space (STS-1, 1981); lost on STS-107 re-entry 2003
